target_customer: Engaged couples (free), monetized via vendor advertising
problem: Finding wedding vendors and planning a wedding was hard and scattered.
business_model: Ad and vendor listing revenue on a wedding planning site

founders.name: Srini Panguluri
founders.background_notes: YC page: two-time YC founder with two exits. No education found.

technical_complexity.rationale: A content and vendor directory site; standard web build.

defensibility.rationale: Community and content gave some pull, but The Knot dominated and listings were easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Incumbents stayed dominant; Project Wedding was sold to WeddingWire in July 2011, formerly an eHarmony property.

market_need_then: Weddings were a large vendor market; The Knot's vendor fee model shows paid demand, but no source measures Project Wedding's own demand at founding.

branding.domain_note: projectwedding.com; acquisition of domain not found

identity.voice_and_tone: Supportive community and editorial, per YC description

branding.community_and_virality: Company claimed over 1 million brides visit monthly at sale in 2011.

brand_strength.rationale: Generic descriptive name; traffic was real but no brand-specific evidence.

outcome_analysis: Project Wedding grew into a planning site with over 1 million monthly visitors and was described at sale as one of the top five wedding destinations. It was owned by eHarmony before WeddingWire bought it on 2011-07-11, with no terms disclosed. A founder-level exit story is not documented in the sources found.
notes: Company site returned 503 so not read. YC says batch W06 while description says started 2007; conflict unresolved. eHarmony as investor appears only on Dealroom, unverified. No funding found, which is not zero. Competitors are dated Aug 2007 press release. Competitor traction and the founder's education not found. The Knot and WeddingChannel were established wedding sites (2007 press release), but no source dated near the batch was found, so the list is empty.
